Sara —

Thanks — this is helpful and aligned with conversations we typically have for private deployments. Attached is a first-pass "witnessing checklist" that we use internally (spreadsheet) and a short list of acceptable evidence types. High-level responses below:  

- License scope: Redwood supports a runtime, non-transferable license scoped to the customer environment in the Order Form (we do not permit sublicensing). We can propose explicit language in the MSA annex to make that clear.
- Witnessing: we can support an escorted, recorded acceptance session where a Redwood engineer performs a snapshot/restore and hands over operator credentials to your designated custodian. We propose limiting this to one witnessed session per major install and logging the session artifacts.
- Audit & access: we provide time-bound audit access windows and a signed attestation post-window. We capture operator actions in immutable logs and can provide redacted extracts.
- Escrow-lite: rather than full source escrow, we typically offer a combination of (a) documented recovery procedures, (b) witnessed snapshot + signed attestation, and (c) optionally a third-party witness for custody transfer.

Next steps: can we schedule a 45-minute call on Tue/Thu next week to walk the checklist with your legal and procurement? I'm looping Karthik (legal ops), Marcus (sales lead for this deal) and Olga (platform security) to review proposed redline language.

Thanks for the ping — see suggested redline snippets and operational constraints below. I've attached a PDF with inline redlines for the MSA annex. High-level guidance: avoid language that creates an open-ended right to copy software or to run it outside customer-owned infrastructure. Keep any witnessing provision bounded (time, scope, and purpose).

Suggested clause snippets (editable):

1) License grant (Order Form / Annex):
"Subject to the terms of this Agreement and the Order Form, Redwood grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to use the Redwood runtime solely on Customer-owned or Customer-controlled compute infrastructure described in the Order Form for Customer internal business purposes. Any transfer, resale, or hosting for third-party use is expressly prohibited without Redwood's prior written consent."

2) Witnessing & acceptance:
"Customer may elect to have a recorded, remote or on-site witnessed acceptance session with a Redwood-designated engineer (\"Witnessing Session\"). The Witnessing Session is limited to validating: (a) successful deployment and basic runtime functionality as specified in Exhibit A, (b) successful snapshot/restore operations required for business continuity. Redwood will retain logs and will provide Customer a signed attestation describing the session scope and outcome. Witnessing Sessions are limited to one per Major Release or as otherwise agreed in writing."

3) Audit & evidence:
"Redwood will provide time-limited access to operational logs and produce a signed attestation describing operator actions during the agreed audit window. Logs will be provided in redacted form to protect Redwood intellectual property and third-party data. Any third-party auditor must execute Redwood's standard NDA and have duties limited to evidence collection only."

Practical constraints / ask items for negotiation:
- Limit witnesses to named individuals or vendor per Exhibit; require NDAs for any third-party auditors.
- Resist language that permits unfettered copying of runtime artifacts; prefer attestations & witnessed restores instead.
- Define "snapshot" and acceptable artifacts (hashes, checksums, logs) to avoid scope creep.

Attachments: redlines_v5.pdf (contains inline MSA annex edits), sample Exhibit A operational checklist.

I'll join the call next week if helpful.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
